source.title: On topological cyclic homology
source.venue: Acta Mathematica 221 (2018), no. 2, 203–409; correction Acta Math. 222 (2019), 215–218
source.version: The published Acta text in its corrected online form (open-access intlpress PDF, 207 pages, created 31 March 2019), read in full; locators and page numbers are the published ones. Also read: the Acta correction (https://www.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/acta/2019/0222/0001/ACTA-2019-0222-0001-a002.pdf, SHA-256 0b98fb63029a31324ad23504f584e3f414b03f4734ba63f49b943b0bd5f27944) and arXiv v2 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1707.01799v2, 7 September 2018, SHA-256 12b6cdbd0d8ebb506284bd13f183affe80e41cc8890fef5fa21c922c2f80cec3), compared at every finding. Pages 332 and 400 were checked on page images.

summary: Nikolaus and Scholze define a cyclotomic spectrum as a spectrum with T-action and T-equivariant Frobenius maps X → X^{tC_p}, with no genuine equivariant homotopy theory, prove that on bounded below spectra this ∞-category is equivalent to the classical genuine one (Theorem II.6.9) and that TC(X) = fib(X^{hT} → ∏_p (X^{tC_p})^{hT}) (Theorems II.4.10–II.4.11), and construct the Frobenius of THH(A) from the Tate diagonal X → (X^{⊗p})^{tC_p}, which they show is a p-completion for bounded below X (Theorem III.1.7). The tools are the Tate orbit lemma, a unique multiplicative structure on Tate constructions via Verdier quotients, a coalgebra argument for endofunctors, and Appendices on symmetric monoidal Dwyer–Kan localisation and cyclic objects; Chapter IV treats the Tate-valued Frobenius (Steenrod and Adams operations), E_∞-rings, loop spaces and TC(F_p). The atlas plans the subject in RefinedTraceMethods RT.2, and neither library has spectra. Routes: RT.2 as the main source (107 items), RT.1 for the HKR filtration, EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5 for the ∞-categorical appendix and Verdier quotients, StableHomotopyKTheory H.1–H.2 for realisations of spaces, KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.5 for THH and TC of F_p, and a Part II of StableHomotopyKTheory for the Segal conjecture and power operations. Complete (cc-442dc5). New findings: Proposition II.3.4's identification of Cyc Sp with a fibre product is false in general; the covering argument for Theorem B.3 has a gap (the statement holds); and a number of misprints, including the Steenrod degree shifts of Theorem IV.1.15 and the p-series of Example I.2.3. The Acta correction's entries are recorded as known. Not formalised.

items.name: Goodwillie's rational comparison (cited)
items.statement: There is a trace map tr: K(A) → HC⁻(A), functorial in A. If A → Ā is a surjection of associative unital algebras with nilpotent kernel, the square formed by K(A)_Q → HC⁻(A⊗Q) and K(Ā)_Q → HC⁻(Ā⊗Q) is homotopy cartesian; (−)_Q is rationalisation.
items.note: Goodwillie [40]; RT.3 plans the rational relative K/cyclic-homology comparison with its nilpotence hypotheses.

items.name: Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy (cited)
items.statement: There is a cyclotomic trace tr: K(A) → TC(A), functorial in A. If A → Ā is a map of connective associative unital algebras in Sp such that π_0A → π_0Ā is surjective with nilpotent kernel, then the square K(A) → TC(A) over K(Ā) → TC(Ā) is homotopy cartesian.
items.note: As printed the surjectivity is omitted (sourceIssues PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18/E3). RT.3 plans the relative nilpotent comparison.

items.name: TC of a connective ring spectrum (Corollary 1.5)
items.statement: For every connective A ∈ Alg_E1(Sp) there is a natural fibre sequence TC(A) → THH(A)^{hT} → ∏_{p∈P} (THH(A)^{tC_p})^{hT}, the second map having p-th component φ_p^{hT} − can, where can: THH(A)^{hT} ≃ (THH(A)^{hC_p})^{h(T/C_p)} = (THH(A)^{hC_p})^{hT} → (THH(A)^{tC_p})^{hT} uses T/C_p ≅ T. Here TC(A) is the classical (genuine) TC of Bökstedt–Hsiang–Madsen and Goodwillie.
items.note: Consequence of Theorems II.4.11 and II.6.9; RT.2 plans the modern formula with its bounded-below hypothesis.

items.name: Pointed, preadditive, additive and stable ∞-categories
items.statement: An ∞-category C is pointed if it has a zero object; preadditive if pointed, with finite products and coproducts, and X ⊔ Y → X × Y (matrix (id, 0; 0, id)) an equivalence for all X, Y; additive if moreover every π_0Hom(X, Y) is a group; stable if additive with all finite limits and colimits and Ω: X ↦ 0 ×_X 0 an equivalence.

items.name: G-equivariant objects
items.statement: For a group G and an ∞-category C, a G-equivariant object is a functor BG → C; C^{BG} = Fun(BG, C). For C = Sp these are spectra with G-action (not genuine G-spectra).

items.name: Homotopy orbits and homotopy fixed points
items.statement: If C has BG-indexed colimits (limits), −_{hG}: C^{BG} → C is colim_BG, and −^{hG}: C^{BG} → C is lim_BG.

items.name: Norms for truncated maps (cited from Higher Algebra)
items.statement: If C is pointed, f_! and f_* exist for every (−1)-truncated map of Kan complexes f: X → Y and Nm_f: f_! → f_* is an equivalence [HA 6.1.6.7]; if C is preadditive, the same holds for 0-truncated maps with finite fibres [HA 6.1.6.12].
items.note: Lemmas I.1.8 and I.1.9 together; the input to the norm construction.

items.name: The norm map of a relative finite groupoid
items.statement: Let C be preadditive with limits and colimits indexed by classifying spaces of finite groups, and f: X → Y a map of Kan complexes whose fibres have finitely many components, each the classifying space of a finite group. Construction I.1.7 produces from the invertible norm Nm_δ of the diagonal δ: X → X ×_Y X a natural transformation Nm_f: f_! → f_* of functors C^X → C^Y (Definition I.1.10). For f: BG → * this is Nm_G: X_{hG} → X^{hG} (Example I.1.11).
items.note: Construction I.1.7, Definition I.1.10, Example I.1.11.

items.name: Equivariance of the norm for a normal subgroup
items.statement: If G is a finite normal subgroup of a topological group H and f: BH → B(H/G), the functors f_!, f_*: C^{BH} → C^{B(H/G)} lift −_{hG} and −^{hG}, and Nm_G: −_{hG} → −^{hG} refines to a natural transformation f_! → f_* of functors C^{BH} → C^{B(H/G)}.

items.name: The Tate construction
items.statement: For C stable with BG-indexed limits and colimits, −^{tG}: C^{BG} → C sends X to cofib(Nm_G: X_{hG} → X^{hG}); for G normal in H, −^{tG}: C^{BH} → C^{B(H/G)} is cofib(Nm_f: f_!X → f_*X). The Tate constructions in R-Mod and in Sp agree.

items.name: Tate spectra of Eilenberg–MacLane spectra
items.statement: For a G-module M, π_i(HM^{tG}) ≅ Ĥ^{−i}(G, M), the Tate cohomology of G; for example Ĥ^*(C_p, Z) ≅ F_p[t^{±1}] with t of degree 2.
items.note: The algebraic side is in the libraries: Mathlib's tateCohomology and tateCohomologyFunctor (a Tate complex built from the norm, at 082e2d3), Tau Ceti's Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.periodicIso and tateCohomologyIsoEven (two-periodicity for cyclic groups, at f790474). The spectrum HM^{tG} and the comparison are absent.

items.name: Tate orbit lemma
items.statement: Let X be a spectrum with C_{p²}-action that is bounded below. Then (X_{hC_p})^{t(C_{p²}/C_p)} ≃ 0.

items.name: Tate fixpoint lemma
items.statement: Let X be a spectrum with C_{p²}-action that is bounded above. Then (X^{hC_p})^{t(C_{p²}/C_p)} ≃ 0.

items.name: The sphere violates the Tate fixpoint lemma
items.statement: For S with trivial C_{p²}-action, (S^{hC_p})^{t(C_{p²}/C_p)} ≃ S_p^∧, the p-completion of S; so S does not satisfy the conclusion of the Tate fixpoint lemma.
items.note: Example I.2.3(i); it uses the Segal conjecture S^{tC_p} ≃ S_p^∧ (Remark III.1.6) and Lemma I.2.9.

items.name: KU violates the Tate orbit lemma
items.statement: For KU with trivial C_{p²}-action, π_*(KU^{tC_p}) ≅ KU_*((x))/((1+x)^p − 1) ≅ KU_* ⊗ Q_p(ζ_p), rational; π_*((KU^{tC_p})^{h(C_{p²}/C_p)}) ≅ KU_* ⊗ Q_p(ζ_p) while π_*(KU^{tC_{p²}}) ≅ KU_*((x))/((1+x)^{p²} − 1) ≅ KU_* ⊗ (Q_p(ζ_p) ⊕ Q_p(ζ_{p²})). Hence (KU^{tC_p})^{h(C_{p²}/C_p)} ≄ KU^{tC_{p²}}, and KU does not satisfy the Tate orbit lemma.
items.note: Example I.2.3(iii), with the p- and p²-series corrected (sourceIssues PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18/E4); uses the Tate spectra of complex oriented theories [41, 5] and KU from RT.4:topological.

items.name: Postnikov pieces of HF_p
items.statement: Let X = HF_p with trivial C_{p²}-action. For every i ≥ 0, (τ_{[2i,2i+1]}X_{hC_p})^{t(C_{p²}/C_p)} ≃ 0 and (τ_{[−2i−1,−2i]}X^{hC_p})^{t(C_{p²}/C_p)} ≃ 0; and X satisfies the conclusions of Lemmas I.2.1 and I.2.2.

items.name: A non-split two-stage complex has vanishing Tate construction
items.statement: Let A ∈ D(F_p)^{BC_p} have only H^0 = H^1 = F_p (with trivial action) and non-zero extension class in π_0Map_{D(F_p)^{BC_p}}(F_p[−1], F_p[1]) = H²(C_p, F_p) = F_p. Then A^{tC_p} ≃ 0.

items.name: Postnikov convergence of orbits, fixed points and Tate
items.statement: For Y a spectrum with action of a finite group G: (i) Y^{hG} → lim_n (τ_{≤n}Y)^{hG}, Y_{hG} → lim_n (τ_{≤n}Y)_{hG} and Y^{tG} → lim_n (τ_{≤n}Y)^{tG} are equivalences; (ii) colim_n (τ_{≥−n}Y)^{hG} → Y^{hG}, colim_n (τ_{≥−n}Y)_{hG} → Y_{hG} and colim_n (τ_{≥−n}Y)^{tG} → Y^{tG} are equivalences.

items.name: Eilenberg–MacLane spectra satisfy both lemmas
items.statement: For an abelian group M with C_{p²}-action, X = HM satisfies the conclusions of Lemmas I.2.1 and I.2.2.

items.name: Tate vanishing when p is invertible
items.statement: If Y is a spectrum with C_p-action on which multiplication by p is an isomorphism on every π_iY, then Y^{tC_p} ≃ 0.

items.name: Tate spectra of bounded below spectra are p-complete
items.statement: If X is a bounded below spectrum with C_p-action, X^{tC_p} is p-complete and X^{tC_p} ≃ (X_p^∧)^{tC_p}.

items.name: Multiplicativity of the Tate construction, with uniqueness
items.statement: For a finite group G, the space of pairs consisting of a lax symmetric monoidal structure on −^{tG}: Sp^{BG} → Sp and a lax symmetric monoidal refinement of the natural transformation −^{hG} → −^{tG} is contractible.
items.note: RT.2 plans 'multiplicative structure' for the Tate construction; the uniqueness, and the construction avoiding genuine equivariant homotopy theory, are new here.

items.name: Stable subcategories and ⊗-ideals
items.statement: A stable subcategory of a stable ∞-category C is a full stable D ⊆ C with exact inclusion; if C is stably symmetric monoidal (⊗ exact in each variable), D is a ⊗-ideal if X ⊗ Y ∈ D for all X ∈ C, Y ∈ D.

items.name: Verdier quotients of stable ∞-categories
items.statement: Let C be small stable and D ⊆ C a stable subcategory, W the maps with cone in D. (i) The Dwyer–Kan localisation C/D = C[W⁻¹] is stable, C → C/D is exact, and for stable E it identifies Fun^Ex(C/D, E) with the exact functors C → E killing D. (ii) Map_{C/D}(X̄, Ȳ) ≃ colim_{Z∈D/Y} Map_C(X, cofib(Z → Y)), a filtered colimit, so the Yoneda functor factors as an exact C/D → Ind(C) sending Ȳ to colim_{Z∈D/Y} cofib(Z → Y). (iii) For presentable stable E, Fun^Ex(C/D, E) ⊆ Fun^Ex(C, E) is right adjoint to a localisation, sending F to C/D → Ind(C) → Ind(E) → E.
items.note: With Lemma I.3.4 (mapping spaces in C[W⁻¹] are L(Map_C(X, −))), proved inside.

items.name: Ind-categories of Verdier quotients
items.statement: For C small stable and D ⊆ C stable, Ind(C) is presentable stable, Ind(D) ⊆ Ind(C) a presentable stable subcategory, and Ind(C) → Ind(C/D) has kernel Ind(D) and is a localisation whose fully faithful right adjoint is the colimit-preserving extension of C/D → Ind(C) of Theorem I.3.3(ii).

items.name: Symmetric monoidal Verdier quotients
items.statement: Let C be small, stably symmetric monoidal and stable and D ⊆ C a stable ⊗-ideal. (i) There is a unique way to make C/D and C → C/D symmetric monoidal, and for symmetric monoidal stable E, Fun^Ex_lax(C/D, E) is the full subcategory of Fun^Ex_lax(C, E) of functors killing D. (ii) If E is presentably symmetric monoidal stable, this inclusion is right adjoint to a localisation given by F ↦ (C/D → Ind(C) → Ind(E) → E), both functors canonically lax symmetric monoidal.

items.name: Induced spectra with G-action
items.statement: Sp^{BG}_ind ⊆ Sp^{BG} is the stable subcategory generated by the spectra ⊕_{g∈G} X with permutation action, X ∈ Sp.

items.name: Properties of induced spectra
items.statement: For X ∈ Sp^{BG}: (i) if X ∈ Sp^{BG}_ind then X^{tG} ≃ 0; (ii) Sp^{BG}_ind ⊆ Sp^{BG} is a ⊗-ideal; (iii) colim_{Y∈(Sp^{BG}_ind)/X} Y → X and colim_{Y∈(Sp^{BG}_ind)/X} cofib(Y → X)^{hG} → X^{tG} are equivalences.

items.name: Residual Tate constructions are lax symmetric monoidal
items.statement: If G is a finite normal subgroup of a topological group H, −^{tG}: Sp^{BH} → Sp^{B(H/G)} has a natural lax symmetric monoidal structure making −^{hG} → −^{tG} lax symmetric monoidal, compatibly with Theorem I.3.1; in particular −^{tC_p}: Sp^{BT} → Sp^{B(T/C_p)}.

items.name: The Tate construction for a Kan complex (Farrell–Tate)
items.statement: For a Kan complex S and p: S → *, with p_! (homology) and p_* (cohomology) adjoint to p*: Sp → Sp^S: (i) Sp^S is compactly generated presentable stable, generated by the compact s_!S (s ∈ S); (ii) there is an initial functor p^T_* with p_* → p^T_* vanishing on compact objects; (iii) it is the unique such functor for which fib(p_* → p^T_*) preserves colimits; (iv) fib(p_* → p^T_*) ≃ p_!(D_S ⊗ −) for a unique D_S ∈ Sp^S, the composite S → Fun(S, S) → Fun(S, Sp) → Sp of Map(−,−), Σ^∞_+ and p_*; (v) p_!(D_S ⊗ −) → p_* is final among colimit-preserving functors over p_* (an assembly map); (vi) if p^T_*(s_!X) ≃ 0 for all s ∈ S and X ∈ Sp, p^T_* has a unique lax symmetric monoidal structure making p_* → p^T_* lax symmetric monoidal.

items.name: The Spivak–Klein dualizing spectrum
items.statement: D_S ∈ Sp^S of Theorem I.4.1(iv); its fibre at s is lim_{t∈S} Σ^∞_+Map(s, t), and for S = BG, D_{BG} = (Σ^∞_+G)^{hG} (Klein).

items.name: The circle norm and T-Tate construction
items.statement: On Sp^{BT} there is a natural transformation Σ(−_{hT}) → −^{hT} exhibiting Σ(−_{hT}) as the universal colimit-preserving functor over −^{hT}; its cofibre −^{tT} has a unique lax symmetric monoidal structure making −^{hT} → −^{tT} lax symmetric monoidal. For n ≥ 1 there is a unique (lax symmetric monoidal) transformation −^{tT} → −^{tC_n} compatible with −^{hT} → −^{hC_n}.
items.note: Uses Klein's computation of D_{BT} [59, Theorem 10.1, Corollary 10.2]. RT.2 plans TP = −^{tT}.

items.name: Integral T-Tate modulo n
items.statement: For HZ with trivial T-action, (HZ)^{tT} → (HZ)^{tC_n} induces π_i(HZ)^{tT}/n ≅ π_i(HZ)^{tC_n} for all i.

items.name: Cyclotomic and p-cyclotomic spectra
items.statement: (i) A cyclotomic spectrum is a spectrum X with T-action together with T ≅ T/C_p-equivariant maps φ_p: X → X^{tC_p} for every prime p (X^{tC_p} with its residual T/C_p-action, identified with T by the p-th power map). (ii) For a prime p, a p-cyclotomic spectrum is a spectrum with C_{p^∞}-action and a C_{p^∞}-equivariant φ_p: X → X^{tC_p}. No compatibility between different φ_p is asked.
items.note: Also Definition 1.3.

items.name: The cyclotomic sphere
items.statement: S with trivial T-action and φ_p: S → S^{hC_p} → S^{tC_p}, made T-equivariant through S → S^{hT} ≃ (S^{hC_p})^{h(T/C_p)} → (S^{tC_p})^{h(T/C_p)}, is a cyclotomic spectrum, equivalent to THH(S); by the Segal conjecture each φ_p is a p-completion.
items.note: Example II.1.2(ii); the p-completion claim is the Segal conjecture of Remark III.1.6 (Part II route).

items.name: Lax equalizers
items.statement: For functors F, G: C → D, LEq(F, G) is the pullback of (ev_0, ev_1): D^{Δ¹} → D × D along (F, G): C → D × D; its objects are pairs (c, f: F(c) → G(c)).

items.name: Properties of lax equalizers
items.statement: (i) The defining pullback is homotopy cartesian. (ii) Map_{LEq}((c_X, f_X), (c_Y, f_Y)) ≃ Eq(Map_C(c_X, c_Y) ⇉ Map_D(F c_X, G c_Y)) via (f_Y)_*F and (f_X)^*G, and a map is an equivalence iff its image in C is. (iii) If C, D are stable and F, G exact, LEq(F, G) is stable and LEq(F, G) → C exact. (iv) If C is presentable, D accessible, F colimit-preserving and G accessible, LEq(F, G) is presentable and LEq(F, G) → C preserves colimits. (v) Limits in C preserved by G lift to LEq(F, G).

items.name: The ∞-categories of cyclotomic spectra
items.statement: (i) Cyc Sp := LEq(Sp^{BT} ⇉ ∏_{p∈P} Sp^{BT}) for id and −^{tC_p}: Sp^{BT} → Sp^{B(T/C_p)} ≃ Sp^{BT}. (ii) Cyc Sp_p := LEq(Sp^{BC_{p^∞}} ⇉ Sp^{BC_{p^∞}}) for id and −^{tC_p}: Sp^{BC_{p^∞}} → Sp^{B(C_{p^∞}/C_p)} ≃ Sp^{BC_{p^∞}}.

items.name: Cyc Sp is presentable stable
items.statement: Cyc Sp and Cyc Sp_p are presentable stable ∞-categories, and the forgetful functors to Sp reflect equivalences, are exact and preserve small colimits.

items.name: TC as a mapping spectrum
items.statement: (i) For a cyclotomic spectrum X, TC(X) = map_{Cyc Sp}(S, X); (ii) for a p-cyclotomic X, TC(X, p) = map_{Cyc Sp_p}(S, X); (iii) for R ∈ Alg_E1(Sp), TC(R) = TC(THH(R)) and TC(R, p) = TC(THH(R), p).

items.name: The fibre sequence for TC
items.statement: (i) For a cyclotomic spectrum X there is a functorial fibre sequence TC(X) → X^{hT} → ∏_p (X^{tC_p})^{hT} with components φ_p^{hT} − can, can: X^{hT} ≃ (X^{hC_p})^{h(T/C_p)} ≃ (X^{hC_p})^{hT} → (X^{tC_p})^{hT}. (ii) For a p-cyclotomic X, TC(X, p) → X^{hC_{p^∞}} → (X^{tC_p})^{hC_{p^∞}} with φ_p^{hC_{p^∞}} − can.

items.name: Orthogonal spectra
items.statement: An orthogonal spectrum is a sequence of pointed spaces X_n with continuous based O(n)-actions and maps σ_n: X_n ∧ S¹ → X_{n+1} whose iterates X_n ∧ S^m → X_{n+m} are O(n) × O(m)-equivariant; π_iX = colim π_{i+n}X_n; a map is a stable equivalence if it induces isomorphisms on all π_i.
items.note: Schwede [85]; neither library has spectra in any model (audit of H.5:spectra).

items.name: Orthogonal G-spectra and geometric fixed points
items.statement: For a finite group G, GSp^O = Fun(BG, Sp^O) with smash product and diagonal action. X(V) = L(R^n, V)_+ ∧_{O(n)} X_n for an n-dimensional representation V; Φ^G X has n-th space X(R^n ⊗ ρ_G)^G (ρ_G the regular representation); f is an equivalence if Φ^H f is a stable equivalence for every H ⊆ G. Φ^G is lax symmetric monoidal and Φ^G X ∧ Φ^G Y → Φ^G(X ∧ Y) is a stable equivalence for cofibrant X, Y [85, Proposition 7.14].
items.note: Definitions II.2.2–II.2.3 and Proposition II.2.4.

items.name: Genuine G-spectra
items.statement: GSp is N(GSp^O) with the equivalences inverted, symmetric monoidal via cofibrant smash; Φ^H: GSp → Sp is the induced symmetric monoidal functor; the genuine fixed points −^H: GSp → Sp come from set-theoretic fixed points of orthogonal G-Ω-spectra, with a lax symmetric monoidal transformation −^H → −^{hH} through GSp → Sp^{BG}.

items.name: Borel-complete genuine spectra
items.statement: GSp → Sp^{BG} has a fully faithful right adjoint B_G whose essential image consists of the X with X^H → X^{hH} an equivalence for all H ⊆ G; B_G is lax symmetric monoidal and id → B_G is a lax symmetric monoidal transformation.
items.note: With Corollary II.2.8.

items.name: Complete universes and the point-set geometric fixed points
items.statement: A complete G-universe U is a countable sum of copies of every irreducible representation. For H ⊆ G normal, Φ^H_U: GSp^O → (G/H)Sp^O has n-th space hocolim_{V∈U, V^H=0} X(R^n ⊕ V)^H (Bousfield–Kan hocolim), and there is a natural zig-zag of stable equivalences Φ^G X → Φ̃^G_U X ← Φ^G_U X.
items.note: Definitions II.2.9–II.2.10 and Lemma II.2.11 (whose proof should read V^G = 0; sourceIssues PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18/E6).

items.name: Geometric fixed points compose
items.statement: For normal subgroups H ⊆ H′ ⊆ G there is a natural map Φ^{H′/H}_{U^H} Φ^H_U X → Φ^{H′}_U X, an equivalence of orthogonal G/H′-spectra.

items.name: Isotropy separation for cyclic p-groups
items.statement: For G cyclic of p-power order and X ∈ GSp there is a natural fibre sequence X_{hG} → X^G → (Φ^{C_p}X)^{G/C_p}; applied to X → B_G X it maps to X_{hG} → X^{hG} → X^{tG}, the right square lax symmetric monoidal, giving −^{tG} a lax symmetric monoidal structure with −^{hG} → −^{tG} lax symmetric monoidal.

items.name: Geometric fixed points as a localisation
items.statement: For H ⊆ G normal, Φ^H: GSp → (G/H)Sp has a fully faithful right adjoint R_H with essential image GSp_{≥H}, the X with X^N ≃ 0 (equivalently Φ^N X ≃ 0) for all N not containing H; on GSp_{≥H}, −^H → Φ^H is an equivalence.

items.name: Genuine C_{p^∞}- and F-genuine T-spectra
items.statement: C_{p^∞}Sp = lim_n C_{p^n}Sp along the forgetful functors; TSp^O the orthogonal spectra with continuous T-action, F-equivalences those inducing equivalences of orthogonal C_n-spectra for every finite C_n ⊆ T, and TSp_F the localisation at them. −^H and Φ^H exist for finite H and satisfy Theorem II.2.7 and Proposition II.2.14.

items.name: Fixed points of R_{C_p}
items.statement: For R_{C_p} on C_{p^∞}Sp or TSp_F, (R_{C_p}X)^H ≃ X^{H/C_p} if C_p ⊆ H and 0 otherwise.

items.name: Genuine p-cyclotomic spectra
items.statement: A genuine p-cyclotomic spectrum is X ∈ C_{p^∞}Sp with an equivalence Φ_p: Φ^{C_p}X ≃ X (via C_{p^∞}/C_p ≅ C_{p^∞}); Cyc Sp_p^gen = Eq(C_{p^∞}Sp ⇉ C_{p^∞}Sp) of id and Φ^{C_p}. Composing Φ_p⁻¹ with Φ^{C_p}X → Φ^{C_p}B(X) gives a functor Cyc Sp_p^gen → Cyc Sp_p.
items.note: With Proposition II.3.2.

items.name: Genuine cyclotomic spectra
items.statement: Cyc Sp^gen = (TSp_F)^{hN_{>0}}, N_{>0} acting by Φ^{C_n}: objects X ∈ TSp_F with coherently commuting equivalences Φ_n: X ≃ Φ^{C_n}X.

items.name: The forgetful functor from genuine to cyclotomic spectra
items.statement: There is a natural functor Cyc Sp^gen → Cyc Sp, sending (X, (Φ_n)) to its underlying spectrum with T-action and the T ≅ T/C_p-equivariant maps X ≃ Φ^{C_p}X → X^{tC_p}.
items.note: As printed the proposition also identifies Cyc Sp with Sp^{BT} ×_{∏Sp^{BC_{p^∞}}} ∏_p Cyc Sp_p, which is false in general (sourceIssues PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18/E1); the functor itself is obtained in §II.6 as Cyc Sp^gen ⊆ CoAlg_{(Φ^{C_p})}(TSp_F) → CoAlg_{(−^{tC_p})}(Sp^{BT}) ≃ Cyc Sp (Lemma II.5.8).

items.name: Orthogonal cyclotomic spectra
items.statement: An orthogonal cyclotomic spectrum is X ∈ TSp^O with F-equivalences Φ_n: Φ^{C_n}_U X → X in TSp^O ≃ (T/C_n)Sp^O for all n ≥ 1 such that Φ_{mn} ∘ (Φ^{C_m}_U Φ^{C_n}_U X ≃ Φ^{C_{mn}}_U X) = Φ_n ∘ Φ^{C_n}_U(Φ_m); maps are equivalences when they are F-equivalences. Cyc Sp^O is their category.

items.name: Orthogonal cyclotomic spectra model genuine ones (cited)
items.statement: N(Cyc Sp^O) → Cyc Sp^gen is the universal functor of ∞-categories inverting the equivalences of orthogonal cyclotomic spectra.
items.note: Barwick–Glasman [11].

items.name: Genuine and naive TC agree; the main equivalence
items.statement: (i) For X ∈ Cyc Sp^gen with bounded below underlying spectrum, TC^gen(X) ≃ TC(X). (ii) For X ∈ Cyc Sp_p^gen bounded below, TC^gen(X, p) ≃ TC(X, p). Moreover Cyc Sp^gen → Cyc Sp and Cyc Sp_p^gen → Cyc Sp_p are equivalences on the full subcategories of bounded below spectra.
items.note: (i)–(ii) are Theorems II.4.11 and II.4.10; the equivalences are Theorems II.6.9 and II.6.3 (also Theorem 1.4).

items.name: Tate construction of C_{p^n} via C_p
items.statement: For bounded below X with C_{p^n}-action, X^{tC_{p^n}} → (X^{tC_p})^{hC_{p^{n−1}}} is an equivalence.

items.name: T-Tate and C_p-Tate
items.statement: For bounded below X with T-action, (X^{tC_p})^{hT} is p-complete and X^{tT} → (X^{tC_p})^{hT} is a p-completion; so ∏_p (X^{tC_p})^{hT} is the profinite completion of X^{tT}.
items.note: With Remark II.4.3.

items.name: TR and genuine TC (Bökstedt–Hsiang–Madsen)
items.statement: For a genuine p-cyclotomic X with restriction R: X^{C_{p^n}} → (Φ^{C_p}X)^{C_{p^{n−1}}} ≃ X^{C_{p^{n−1}}} and inclusion F: X^{C_{p^n}} → X^{C_{p^{n−1}}}, TR(X, p) = lim_R X^{C_{p^n}} and TC^gen(X, p) = Eq(TR(X, p) ⇉ TR(X, p)) (id, F) ≃ lim Eq(X^{C_{p^n}} ⇉ X^{C_{p^{n−1}}}) (R, F); TC^gen(X) for genuine cyclotomic X is defined by diagram (1) over all n.

items.name: The restriction pullback
items.statement: For a genuine C_{p^n}-spectrum X and n ≥ 1 there is a natural pullback square with X^{C_{p^n}} → (Φ^{C_p}X)^{C_{p^{n−1}}} over X^{hC_{p^n}} → X^{tC_{p^n}}.

items.name: Fixed points of bounded below genuine C_{p^n}-spectra
items.statement: If the underlying spectrum of a genuine C_{p^n}-spectrum X is bounded below, there is a canonical pullback square X^{C_{p^n}} → (Φ^{C_p}X)^{C_{p^{n−1}}} over X^{hC_{p^n}} → (X^{tC_p})^{hC_{p^{n−1}}}.

items.name: Iterated pullback for genuine fixed points
items.statement: If X, Φ^{C_p}X, …, Φ^{C_{p^{n−1}}}X are bounded below, X^{C_{p^n}} is the iterated pullback of the diagram with (Φ^{C_{p^i}}X)^{hC_{p^{n−i}}} → ((Φ^{C_{p^{i−1}}}X)^{tC_p})^{hC_{p^{n−i}}} ← … ending in Φ^{C_{p^n}}X → (Φ^{C_{p^{n−1}}}X)^{tC_p}.

items.name: Segal-conjecture reduction from C_{p^n} to C_p
items.statement: Let X be a genuine C_{p^n}-spectrum such that each Y ∈ {X, Φ^{C_p}X, …, Φ^{C_{p^{n−1}}}X} is bounded below and (Y^{C_p})_p^∧ → (Y^{hC_p})_p^∧ is an isomorphism on π_i for i ≥ k. Then (X^{C_{p^n}})_p^∧ → (X^{hC_{p^n}})_p^∧ is an isomorphism on π_i for i ≥ k.
items.note: Generalises Ravenel, Tsalidis and Bökstedt–Bruner–Lunøe-Nielsen–Rognes [21, Theorem 2.5] (no finite-type hypothesis). BMS19 routed Tsalidis's theorem to RT.2.

items.name: Genuine p-typical TC is the modern one
items.statement: For a genuine p-cyclotomic X with bounded below underlying spectrum there is a canonical fibre sequence TC^gen(X, p) → X^{hC_{p^∞}} → (X^{tC_p})^{hC_{p^∞}} (φ_p^{hC_{p^∞}} − can); hence TC^gen(X, p) ≃ TC(X, p).

items.name: Genuine integral TC is the modern one
items.statement: For a genuine cyclotomic X with bounded below underlying spectrum there is a canonical fibre sequence TC^gen(X) → X^{hT} → ∏_p (X^{tC_p})^{hT} ((φ_p^{hT} − can)_p); hence TC^gen(X) ≃ TC(X).

items.name: Coalgebras and fixed points of endofunctors
items.statement: For F: C → C, an F-coalgebra is X with X → FX, a fixpoint one with X ≃ FX; CoAlg_F(C) = LEq(C ⇉ C) of id and F, and Fix_F ⊆ CoAlg_F is the full subcategory of fixpoints. For commuting endofunctors (F_i)_{i∈N}, CoAlg_{(F_i)}(C) and Fix_{(F_i)}(C) are defined iteratively.
items.note: With Remark II.5.7.

items.name: The shifted coalgebra and its right adjoint
items.statement: F̄: CoAlg_F → CoAlg_F sends (X → FX) to (FX → F²X), with µ: id → F̄. If C is presentable and F preserves colimits, Fix_F ⊆ CoAlg_F preserves colimits and has a right adjoint R_ι, and F̄ has a right adjoint R_F with ν: R_F → id.

items.name: The coreflection onto fixed points
items.statement: ιR_ι: CoAlg_F → CoAlg_F is the limit of … → R_F³ → R_F² → R_F → id (maps R_F^kν).

items.name: Formula for R_F
items.statement: If F has a fully faithful right adjoint R_F (unit η), R_F sends a coalgebra φ: X → FX to Y = X ×_{R_F F X} R_F X (along η_X and R_Fφ) with structure Y → X ≃ F R_F X ≅ FY; the counit F R_F → id is an equivalence. The k-fold iterate has underlying object R_F^k X ×_{R_F^k F X} R_F^{k−1}X ×_{R_F^{k−1}FX} … ×_{R_F F X} X.
items.note: With Corollary II.5.5.

items.name: Genuine p-cyclotomic spectra coreflect
items.statement: ι: Cyc Sp_p^gen ⊆ CoAlg_{Φ^{C_p}}(C_{p^∞}Sp) has a right adjoint R_ι whose counit ιR_ι → id is an equivalence on underlying non-equivariant spectra.

items.name: Coalgebras for endofunctors with terminal composites
items.statement: Let C be presentable with commuting accessible F_i preserving the terminal object. (i) If F_i F_j X is terminal for all i ≠ j, (F_i)-coalgebra structures on X correspond to families φ_i: X → F_iX. (ii) Then Map(Y, X) is Eq(Map_C(Y, X) ⇉ ∏_i Map_C(Y, F_iX)). (iii) If F_iF_j is always terminal, CoAlg_{(F_i)}(C) ≃ LEq(C ⇉ ∏_i C) of (id, id, …) and (F_1, F_2, …).

items.name: Fixed points of commuting endofunctors
items.statement: For commuting endofunctors (F_1, F_2, …) of C, Fix_{(F_i)}(C) ≃ C^{hN_{>0}}.

items.name: Coreflection one prime at a time
items.statement: ι_n: Fix_{F_1..F_n}(CoAlg_{F_{n+1},…}) ⊆ Fix_{F_1..F_{n−1}}(CoAlg_{F_n,…}) has ι_nR_{ι_n} = lim(… → R_{F_n}² → R_{F_n} → id); if each F_n has a fully faithful right adjoint with F_iR_{F_n} ≃ R_{F_n}F_i (i ≠ n) and all F_i preserve pullbacks, R_{F_n}^k X has the iterated-pullback formula of Lemma II.5.4.
items.note: Lemmas II.5.10 and II.5.11.

items.name: Geometric fixed points commute with R_{C_q}
items.statement: Φ^{C_p}R_{C_q} → R_{C_q}Φ^{C_p} is an equivalence of endofunctors of TSp_F for primes p ≠ q.

items.name: Genuine cyclotomic spectra coreflect
items.statement: ι: Cyc Sp^gen ≃ Fix_{(Φ^{C_p})_p}(TSp_F) ⊆ CoAlg_{(Φ^{C_p})_p}(TSp_F) has a right adjoint R_ι whose counit induces an equivalence on underlying spectra.

items.name: Φ^{C_p} preserves Borel-completeness (bounded below)
items.statement: If X ∈ C_{p^∞}Sp is Borel complete with bounded below underlying spectrum, Φ^{C_p}X is Borel complete; so Φ^{C_p}B_{C_{p^∞}}Y ≃ B_{C_{p^∞}}(Y^{tC_p}) for bounded below Y with C_{p^∞}-action.
items.note: The non-formal input, from the Tate orbit lemma.

items.name: The right adjoint on bounded below p-cyclotomic spectra
items.statement: For bounded below (X, φ_p) ∈ Cyc Sp_p, the right adjoint B: Cyc Sp_p → CoAlg_{Φ^{C_p}}(C_{p^∞}Sp) of the forgetful functor is B_{C_{p^∞}}X with B_{C_{p^∞}}φ_p: B X → B(X^{tC_p}) ≃ Φ^{C_p}(B X); the counit UB(X, φ) → (X, φ) is an equivalence.

items.name: Genuine and naive p-cyclotomic spectra agree (bounded below)
items.statement: Cyc Sp_p^gen → Cyc Sp_p is an equivalence between the full subcategories of objects with bounded below underlying spectra.

items.name: Borel completeness for F-genuine T-spectra
items.statement: If X ∈ TSp_F is Borel complete with bounded below underlying spectrum, Φ^{C_p}X is Borel complete for every p; and a Borel complete G-spectrum X for a finite group G that is not a p-group has Φ^G X ≃ 0.
items.note: Lemmas II.6.6 and II.6.7.

items.name: The right adjoint on bounded below cyclotomic spectra
items.statement: For bounded below X ∈ Cyc Sp, the right adjoint B: Cyc Sp → CoAlg_{(Φ^{C_p})}(TSp_F) has underlying object the Borel complete B_T X, and the counit UB(X, φ) → (X, φ) is an equivalence.

items.name: Main theorem: genuine and naive cyclotomic spectra agree (bounded below)
items.statement: The forgetful functor Cyc Sp^gen → Cyc Sp induces an equivalence between the full subcategories of objects whose underlying non-equivariant spectra are bounded below.
items.note: Theorem 1.4 of the introduction. RT.2 plans agreement of TC with the classical formulation, not this equivalence of ∞-categories.

items.name: T_p is exact
items.statement: For a prime p, T_p: Sp → Sp, X ↦ (X ⊗ … ⊗ X)^{tC_p} (p factors, C_p permuting cyclically) is exact.

items.name: Transformations out of the identity of Sp
items.statement: For exact F: Sp → Sp, evaluation at S gives Map_{Fun^Ex(Sp,Sp)}(id, F) ≃ Hom_Sp(S, F(S)) = Ω^∞F(S); in particular natural transformations id → T_p correspond to Ω^∞T_p(S).
items.note: With Corollary III.1.3.

items.name: The Tate diagonal
items.statement: Δ_p: id_Sp → T_p, X → (X ⊗ … ⊗ X)^{tC_p}, is the transformation corresponding under Proposition III.1.2 to S → S^{hC_p} → S^{tC_p} = T_p(S).
items.note: Equivalent to the construction of the Hill–Hopkins–Ravenel norm for C_p and to Lunøe-Nielsen–Rognes's topological Singer construction (Remark III.1.5).

items.name: The Segal conjecture for C_p (cited)
items.statement: Δ_p(S): S → S^{tC_p} exhibits S^{tC_p} as the p-completion of S; in particular S^{tC_p} is connective.
items.note: Lin (p = 2) [66], Gunawardena (p odd) [44]; the base case to which the general Segal conjecture reduces [25].

items.name: The base case HF_p (cited)
items.statement: HF_p → T_p(HF_p) = (HF_p ⊗ … ⊗ HF_p)^{tC_p} is an equivalence.
items.note: Lunøe-Nielsen–Rognes [80], a calculation with an Adams-type spectral sequence; for p = 2 also Jones–Wegmann [56].

items.name: The generalised Segal conjecture for C_p
items.statement: For every bounded below X ∈ Sp, Δ_p: X → (X ⊗ … ⊗ X)^{tC_p} exhibits the target as the p-completion of X. It fails without the bounded below hypothesis: (KU ⊗ KU)^{tC_2} is rational.
items.note: Theorem 1.7 of the introduction (second half). Proved from the HF_p case by Postnikov truncation, Lemma I.2.6 and Lemma III.1.8.

items.name: Pro-isomorphism for finite towers
items.statement: If (S_n)_{n≥0} is a tower of finite sets with S_∞ = lim_n S_n finite, then the constant tower (S_∞) → (S_n) is a pro-isomorphism.

items.name: No Tate diagonal in D(Z)
items.statement: Every natural transformation C → (C ⊗_Z … ⊗_Z C)^{tC_p} of functors D(Z) → D(Z) induces zero on homology H_*(C) → Ĥ^{−*}(C_p; C ⊗_Z … ⊗_Z C); in particular there is no lax symmetric monoidal such transformation.

items.name: E_1-algebras and the Segal description
items.statement: Alg_E1(Sp) is the ∞-category of ∞-operad maps N(Ass^⊗) → Sp^⊗; restriction along Δ^op → Ass^⊗ identifies it with functors N(Δ^op) → Sp^⊗ over N(Fin_*) satisfying the Segal condition (each ρ_i: A^⊗([n]) → A^⊗([1]) = A an equivalence onto the i-th factor).
items.note: With Proposition III.2.2; E5:abstract plans operadic algebras and Segal conditions.

items.name: THH of an E_1-ring
items.statement: For A ∈ Alg_E1(Sp), THH(A) ∈ Sp^{BT} is the geometric realisation (Proposition B.5) of the cyclic spectrum N(Λ^op) → N(Ass^⊗_act) → Sp^⊗_act → Sp, the last functor the tensor product, the first V^op (Proposition B.1).

items.name: The cyclotomic Frobenius of THH
items.statement: The Tate diagonals A^{⊗n} → (A^{⊗pn})^{tC_p} assemble, via the subdivision sd_p: Λ_p → Λ and the functors on N(Free_{C_p}) ×_{N(Fin)} Sp^⊗_act, into a map of Λ_p^op-spectra whose realisation is a T ≅ T/C_p-equivariant φ_p: THH(A) → THH(A)^{tC_p} for every p, making THH: Alg_E1(Sp) → Cyc Sp a functor.
items.note: Uses Proposition B.20 to compare the Tate construction with the realisation.

items.name: The Tate diagonal is uniquely lax symmetric monoidal
items.statement: With T_p lax symmetric monoidal by Theorem I.3.1, there is a unique lax symmetric monoidal transformation Δ_p: id_Sp → T_p, with underlying transformation that of Definition III.1.4.
items.note: Theorem 1.7 (first half); uses Nikolaus's uniqueness [81, Corollary 6.9].

items.name: Lax functors and the active part
items.statement: For symmetric monoidal C, D, restriction along C ⊆ C^⊗_act is an equivalence Fun_⊗(C^⊗_act, D) ≃ Fun_lax(C, D); the inclusion Fun_⊗(C^⊗_act, D) ⊆ Fun_lax(C^⊗_act, D) has a right adjoint which, composed with this equivalence, is restriction along C → C^⊗_act; the same holds for any ∞-operad O^⊗ with envelope O^⊗_act.
items.note: Proposition III.3.2, Lemma III.3.3, Remarks III.3.4–III.3.5.

items.name: The C_p-equivariant p-fold tensor functor
items.statement: For symmetric monoidal C and p ≥ 1 there is a natural symmetric monoidal functor N(Free_{C_p}) ×_{N(Fin)} C^⊗_act → (C^⊗_act)^{BC_p}, (S, (X_s̄)_{s̄∈S̄}) ↦ (S, (X_s̄)_{s∈S}).
items.note: The published proof as corrected uses the pointwise tensor product (sourceIssues PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18/E24).

items.name: Initiality of the tensor functor
items.statement: I: N(Free_{C_p}) ×_{N(Fin)} Sp^⊗_act → Sp, (S, (X_s̄)) ↦ ⊗_{s̄∈S̄} X_s̄, is initial among partially exact lax symmetric monoidal functors; hence T̃_p: (S, (X_s̄)) ↦ (⊗_{s∈S} X_s̄)^{tC_p} receives an essentially unique BC_p-equivariant lax symmetric monoidal transformation from I.
items.note: With Corollary III.3.8.

items.name: Bökstedt's category I and the approximation lemma
items.statement: I is the category of finite sets and injections (symmetric monoidal under ⊔). If F: I^n → S sends all maps of the full subcategory I^n_x of objects under x to k-connected maps, then F(x) → colim_{I^n} F is k-connected.
items.note: Definition III.4.1 and Lemma III.4.2 [32, Lemma 2.2.3].

items.name: The Bökstedt construction
items.statement: B: (Sp^O)^⊗_act → Sp^O, the lax symmetric monoidal functor sending (X_i)_{i∈I} to the orthogonal spectrum with n-th space hocolim_{(I_i)∈I^I} Map_*(∧_i S^{I_i}, S^n ∧ ∧_i (X_i)_{I_i}).

items.name: B preserves stable equivalences (Shipley)
items.statement: B takes stable equivalences (maps over a bijection of index sets that are levelwise stable equivalences) to stable equivalences.

items.name: The Bökstedt construction models the tensor product
items.statement: There is a unique (up to contractible choice) transformation of lax symmetric monoidal functors ⊗ → B: Sp^⊗_act → Sp, and it is an equivalence.

items.name: Geometric fixed points of the Bökstedt construction
items.statement: For a finite free C_p-set S with S̄ = S/C_p and orthogonal spectra (X_s̄), the natural map (Construction III.4.6) Φ^{C_p}_U B((X_s̄)_{s∈S}) → B((X_s̄)_{s̄∈S̄}) is a stable equivalence.
items.note: Essentially Hesselholt–Madsen [47, Proposition 2.5].

items.name: Classical THH of an orthogonal ring spectrum
items.statement: For an orthogonal ring spectrum R and a pointed space X, THH(R; X) is the realisation of the cyclic space [k]_Λ ↦ hocolim_{(I_1..I_k)∈I^k} Map_*(S^{I_1} ∧ … ∧ S^{I_k}, X ∧ R_{I_1} ∧ … ∧ R_{I_k}); THH(R) ∈ TSp^O has m-th space THH(R; S^m). If R is levelwise well pointed and S⁰ → R_0 is an h-cofibration, these cyclic spaces are proper.
items.note: With Lemma III.5.2 [68, Lemma 6.17].

items.name: Classical THH is an orthogonal cyclotomic spectrum
items.statement: Φ^{C_p}_U THH(R) is homeomorphic to the realisation of the Λ_p^op-spectrum built from B_p (Propositions III.5.4, III.5.5, T-equivariantly), THH(R) to that built from B (Proposition III.5.6), and Construction III.4.6 gives Φ_p: Φ^{C_p}_U THH(R) → THH(R), F-equivalences satisfying Definition II.3.6.

items.name: Comparison of the two THH
items.statement: For an orthogonal ring spectrum R, levelwise well pointed with S⁰ → R_0 an h-cofibration, the classical THH(R) is naturally T-equivariantly equivalent to THH(A) of the associated E_1-ring A: a commutative square of lax symmetric monoidal functors N Alg(Sp^O)_well → N TSp^O over Alg_E1(Sp) → Sp^{BT} whose vertical functors are Dwyer–Kan localisations.

items.name: Models of geometric fixed points
items.statement: Φ^{C_p}_∞: C_pSp → Sp is the BC_p-equivariant symmetric monoidal composite of the smashing localisation C_pSp → C_pSp_{≥C_p} and −^{C_p}; Φ^{C_p}_{U,lax}: C_pSp^O → TSp^O (hocolim over I and (V_i) ∈ U^I with V_i^{C_p} = 0) is BC_p-equivariant and lax symmetric monoidal and receives stable equivalences from Φ^{C_p}_U and Φ^{C_p}; the square comparing Φ^{C_p}_{U,lax} with Φ^{C_p}_∞ commutes BC_p-equivariantly and lax symmetric monoidally.
items.note: Constructions III.6.2–III.6.5 and Proposition III.6.6.

items.name: Uniqueness for the comparison of Frobenii
items.statement: B^T_{p,lax}, B_{p,∞}, B, I and T̃_p composed with the forgetful functors to Sp^{BT} factor uniquely through BC_p-equivariant lax symmetric monoidal partially exact functors N(Free_{C_p}) ×_{N(Fin)} Sp^⊗_act → Sp^{BT}, among which I is initial.

items.name: The two cyclotomic structures agree
items.statement: For R as in Theorem III.6.1, under its equivalence the classical and the Tate-diagonal cyclotomic Frobenii THH(A) → THH(A)^{tC_p} are equivalent, functorially in R.

items.name: The Tate-valued Frobenius
items.statement: For an E_∞-ring R and a prime p, φ_R: R → (R ⊗ … ⊗ R)^{tC_p} → R^{tC_p} is the composite of the Tate diagonal and m^{tC_p}, m: R^{⊗p} → R the C_p-equivariant multiplication; an E_∞-ring map.

items.name: The Tate-valued Frobenius on π_0 and for spherical Witt vectors
items.statement: (i) For R = HA, A commutative, φ on π_0 is A → A/p = Ĥ⁰(C_p, A), a ↦ a^p. (ii) For p-complete R compact among p-complete spectra, R → R^{hC_p} → R^{tC_p} is an equivalence (Segal conjecture), so φ_R is an E_∞-endomorphism; for S_p^∧ it is the identity, and for the p-complete étale S_p^∧-algebra S_{W(F_{p^n})} it is the unique E_∞-map inducing the Witt-vector Frobenius on π_0.
items.note: Mathlib has the ring-level Frobenius (frobenius) and the Witt-vector Frobenius (WittVector.frobenius) at 082e2d3; the spectra are absent.

items.name: Refinements of the Tate diagonal
items.statement: Δ_p factors uniquely, lax symmetric monoidally, through ((X ⊗ … ⊗ X)^{tC_p})^{hF_p^×} (F_p^× = Aut(C_p), the Weyl group of C_p in Σ_p), and for X = Σ^∞_+Y through Σ^∞_+Δ: Σ^∞_+Y → (Σ^∞_+Y ⊗ … ⊗ Σ^∞_+Y)^{hΣ_p}. Hence φ_R factors as an E_∞-map through (R^{tC_p})^{hF_p^×}, and for R = S[M], M an E_∞-monoid, through (R^{hC_p})^{hF_p^×}.
items.note: Lemma IV.1.3, Corollaries IV.1.4–IV.1.5.

items.name: The space-level diagonal factors the Tate diagonal
items.statement: Ω^∞(Δ_p): Ω^∞ → Ω^∞T_p^{hF_p^×} factors naturally as Ω^∞X → ((Ω^∞X)^{×p})^{hΣ_p} → Ω^∞(X^{⊗p})^{hΣ_p} → Ω^∞((X^{⊗p})^{hC_p})^{hF_p^×} → Ω^∞T_p(X)^{hF_p^×}.

items.name: Homotopy fixed points of p-th tensor powers
items.statement: For X bounded below and p-complete and i ≥ 1, π_i((X ⊗ … ⊗ X)^{hC_p}) ≅ π_i(X) ⊕ π_i((X ⊗ … ⊗ X)_{hC_p}) via the norm and the space-level diagonal, and 0 → π_0((X^{⊗p})_{hC_p}) → π_0((X^{⊗p})^{hC_p}) → π_0(X) → 0 is exact.

items.name: The Tate-valued Frobenius is a power operation
items.statement: For an E_∞-ring R, φ factors on multiplicative E_∞-monoids as Ω^∞R → (Ω^∞R)^{hΣ_p} → Ω^∞(R^{tC_p})^{hF_p^×} (P_p = multiplication ∘ diagonal); on a space X, postcomposition with φ is R⁰(X) → R⁰(X × BΣ_p) = [Σ^∞_+X, R^{hΣ_p}] → [Σ^∞_+X, (R^{tC_p})^{hF_p^×}] with P_p the power operation, so R⁰(X) → R⁰(X × BΣ_p)/I (I the transfer ideal) → [Σ^∞_+X, R^{tC_p}] commutes.
items.note: Corollaries IV.1.9–IV.1.10 and Remark IV.1.11 (whose R⁰(BΣ_p) should read R⁰(X × BΣ_p); sourceIssues PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18/E9).

items.name: The Tate-valued Frobenius of KU is the Adams operation
items.statement: (KU^{tC_p})^{hF_p^×} ≃ KU_p^∧[1/p] (and ((KU^X)^{tC_p})^{hF_p^×} ≃ (KU^X)_p^∧[1/p]). (i) For compact X, φ on π_0 is KU⁰(X) → KU⁰(X) ⊗ Q_p, V ↦ ψ^p(V). (ii) φ_p: KU → KU_p^∧[1/p] is the stable Adams operation ψ^p: KU → KU[1/p] followed by completion; it sends β to pβ.
items.note: Via Atiyah's cyclic power operation [7]; Remark IV.1.14 gives a splitting-principle proof. KU is planned in RT.4:topological.

items.name: The Tate-valued Frobenius of HF_p is the total Steenrod operation
items.statement: φ: HF_p → (HF_p^{tC_p})^{hF_p^×} is, as a map of spectra, the product of the Sq^i: HF_2 → HF_2[i] (i ≥ 0) for p = 2, and of P^i: HF_p → HF_p[2i(p−1)] and βP^i: HF_p → HF_p[2i(p−1)+1] (i ≥ 0) for odd p; for HZ it is the product of the Sq^{2i}r (p = 2) or the P^i r (p odd), r: HZ → HF_p. On a space X: x ↦ Σ_i Sq^i(x)s^i in H^*(X; F_2)((s)), and x ↦ Σ_i P^i(x)t^{(p−1)i} + Σ_i βP^i(x)t^{(p−1)i}e in H^*(X; F_p)((t^{p−1})) ⊗ Λ(e), |t^{p−1}| = −2(p−1), |e| = −1.
items.note: Theorem IV.1.15 with Proposition IV.1.16; the printed shifts [i(p−1)], [n(p−1)] are corrected (sourceIssues PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18/E5).

items.name: Suspensions of the Tate construction
items.statement: For an E_∞-ring R and n ∈ Z, Σ^n(R^{tC_p})^{hF_p^×} ≃ ((Σ^{n·ρ}R)^{tC_p})^{hF_p^×}, ρ the permutation representation of Σ_p; and the square with Ω^∞Σ^nφ_R, P^n_p: Ω^∞Σ^nR → Ω^∞(Σ^{n·ρ}R)^{hΣ_p} and can commutes.
items.note: Lemmas IV.1.17–IV.1.18.

items.name: Power operations in positive degree
items.statement: R^{n·ρ}(X × BΣ_p) := [(X × BΣ_p)^{−n·ρ}, R] ≅ [Σ^∞_+X, (Σ^{n·ρ}R)^{hΣ_p}] (Thom spectra via parametrised spectra); Rezk's power operation P^n_p: R^n(X) → R^{n·ρ}(X × BΣ_p) is postcomposition with P^n_p; and postcomposition with Σ^nφ_R is R^n(X) → R^{n·ρ}(BΣ_p × X) ≅ [Σ^∞_+X, (Σ^{n·ρ}R)^{hΣ_p}] → [Σ^∞_+X, Σ^n(R^{tC_p})^{hF_p^×}].
items.note: Lemmas IV.1.19–IV.1.20 and Theorem IV.1.21.

items.name: Symmetric monoidal structure on cyclotomic spectra
items.statement: Cyc Sp and Cyc Sp_p are symmetric monoidal: C^S = Fun(S, C) is symmetric monoidal for symmetric monoidal C, and LEq(F, G) is symmetric monoidal for F symmetric monoidal and G lax symmetric monoidal. THH: Alg_E1(Sp) → Cyc Sp is symmetric monoidal, so for an E_∞-ring A, THH(A) is an E_∞-algebra in Cyc Sp, and A → THH(A), Δ_p and φ_p form a commutative square of E_∞-rings.

items.name: THH of an E_∞-ring is the tensor with the circle (McClure–Schwänzl–Vogt)
items.statement: For an E_∞-ring A, A → THH(A) is initial among E_∞-maps from A to E_∞-rings with T-action.

items.name: The Frobenius of an E_∞-ring
items.statement: For an E_∞-ring A, φ_p is the unique T-equivariant E_∞-map THH(A) → THH(A)^{tC_p} making the square with A → THH(A), Δ_p and (A ⊗ … ⊗ A)^{tC_p} → THH(A)^{tC_p} commute; and A → THH(A) → THH(A)^{tC_p} → A^{tC_p} (π^{tC_p}, π the retraction) is the Tate-valued Frobenius.
items.note: Corollaries IV.2.3–IV.2.4 and Lurie's equivariant description.

items.name: Cyclotomic structure on cyclic bar constructions
items.statement: For an E_1-monoid M in spaces, B^cyc M has a T-action and T-equivariant ψ_p: B^cyc M → (B^cyc M)^{hC_p} compatible with the diagonal M → (M^{×p})^{hC_p}; Σ^∞_+ψ_p followed by can refines φ_p on THH(S[M]) = Σ^∞_+B^cyc M.

items.name: Cyclic bar construction of a loop space
items.statement: For connected based Y, B^cyc ΩY ≃ LY = Map(S¹, Y) T-equivariantly, and ψ_p becomes LY → LY^{hC_p} induced by the p-fold covering S¹ → S¹. Hence THH(S[ΩY]) ≃ Σ^∞_+LY with φ_p: Σ^∞_+LY → (Σ^∞_+LY)^{hC_p} → (Σ^∞_+LY)^{tC_p}.
items.note: Proposition IV.3.2 and Corollary IV.3.3.

items.name: TC with a Frobenius lift
items.statement: For a bounded below p-complete p-cyclotomic X with a C_{p^∞}-equivariant Frobenius lift φ̃_p: X → X^{hC_p}, TC(X) is the pullback of ΣX_{hT} → X (tr) along id − φ̃_p: X → X; for p-complete X the square X^{hT} → X^{hT} (id − φ̃_p^{hT}) over X → X (id − φ̃_p) is a pullback.
items.note: Proposition IV.3.4 and Lemma IV.3.5.

items.name: TC of spherical group rings (Bökstedt–Hsiang–Madsen)
items.statement: For a connected based space Y, after p-completion TC(S[ΩY]) is the pullback of Σ(Σ^∞_+LY)_{hT} → Σ^∞_+LY (tr) along 1 − φ̃_p: Σ^∞_+LY → Σ^∞_+LY.

items.name: The Segal conjecture for free loop spaces
items.statement: For simply connected Y, the Frobenius φ_p: Σ^∞_+LY → (Σ^∞_+LY)^{tC_p} of THH(S[ΩY]) is a p-completion, and (Σ^∞_+LY)^{C_{p^n}} → (Σ^∞_+LY)^{hC_{p^n}} is a p-adic equivalence for every n.
items.note: Generalises Carlsson [26] (finite simply connected CW complexes); uses Kuhn's convergence [63] and Theorem III.1.7.

items.name: The HKR filtration
items.statement: For a commutative ring A, HH(A) = HH(A/Z) has a descending separated filtration with graded pieces (∧^i L_{A/Z})[i], exterior powers derived.
items.note: RT.1 plans HKR for smooth algebras in characteristic 0; cotangent complexes and derived exterior powers are planned in DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0.

items.name: THH and HH agree in low degrees
items.statement: For an associative unital ring A, π_i THH(HA) → H_i HH(A) is an isomorphism for i ≤ 2.

items.name: Hochschild homology of F_p
items.statement: H_i HH(F_p) is F_p for even i ≥ 0 and 0 otherwise; H_*HH(F_p) is the divided power algebra on u ∈ H_2HH(F_p) over F_p.

items.name: Bökstedt periodicity (cited)
items.statement: π_i THH(HF_p) is F_p for even i ≥ 0 and 0 otherwise, and π_*THH(HF_p) = F_p[u], |u| = 2.
items.note: Bökstedt; Remark IV.4.5 recalls the Mahowald–Hopkins proof via HF_p as a Thom spectrum over Ω²S³ [16, 17]. BMS19 marked Bökstedt periodicity planned in L.5 and RT.2.

items.name: Negative topological cyclic homology of F_p
items.statement: π_*THH(HF_p)^{hT} = Z_p[ũ, v]/(ũv − p), |ũ| = 2, |v| = −2; in degree 2 the image of p in H²(BT, π_2THH(HF_p)) is uv.
items.note: Proposition IV.4.6 and Lemma IV.4.7.

items.name: Periodic topological cyclic homology of F_p and its Frobenius
items.statement: π_*THH(HF_p)^{tT} = Z_p[v^{±1}]; can: π_iTHH(HF_p)^{hT} → π_iTHH(HF_p)^{tT} is an isomorphism for i ≤ 0 and has image p^jZ_p for i = 2j ≥ 0; φ_p^{hT} is an isomorphism for i ≥ 0 and has image p^jZ_p for i = −2j ≤ 0.
items.note: Corollary IV.4.8 and Proposition IV.4.9.

items.name: TC of F_p
items.statement: π_iTC(HF_p) = Z_p for i = 0, −1 and 0 otherwise; THH(HF_p) is a T-equivariant τ_{≥0}TC(HF_p) = HZ_p-algebra and φ_p is a map of E_∞-HZ_p-algebras.

items.name: T-equivariant chain complexes and Tate constructions
items.statement: For X ∈ D(Z)^{BT}: X^{hT} ⊗_{Z^{hT}} Z ≃ X, X^{hT} ⊗_{Z^{hT}} Z^{tT} ≃ X^{tT}, and X^{tT} ⊗_{Z^{tT}} Z^{tC_n} ≃ X^{tC_n} for n ≥ 1.

items.name: THH(F_p) as a cyclotomic E_∞-ring
items.statement: HZ_p → THH(HF_p) induces an equivalence of E_∞-algebras HZ_p^{tC_p} ≃ THH(HF_p)^{tC_p}, so π_*THH(HF_p)^{tC_p} ≅ F_p[v^{±1}], and φ_p identifies THH(HF_p) with τ_{≥0}THH(HF_p)^{tC_p} ≃ τ_{≥0}HZ_p^{tC_p}.

items.name: Trivial cyclotomic structures are left adjoint to TC
items.statement: X ↦ X^triv (trivial T-action, Frobenius X → X^{hC_p} → X^{tC_p}) is left adjoint to TC: Cyc Sp → Sp.

items.name: THH(F_p) ≃ sh_p(HZ_p^triv)
items.statement: For connective cyclotomic X, sh_pX is τ_{≥0}(X^{tC_p}) with residual action and Frobenius induced by φ_p (Construction IV.4.15), with a map X → sh_pX. In the square from HZ_p^triv → THH(F_p), the right and lower maps are equivalences of E_∞-cyclotomic spectra, so THH(F_p) ≃ sh_p(HZ_p^triv); ũ, v can be chosen with ũv = p and φ_p^{hT}(v) = pv, the constants λ_n of [47, Proposition 5.4] can be 1, and THH(HF_p)^{C_{p^n}} ≃ τ_{≥0}HZ_p^{tC_{p^{n+1}}}.
items.note: Construction IV.4.15 and Corollary IV.4.16; Remark IV.4.17 notes three different E_∞-maps HZ_p → HZ_p^{tC_p}.

items.name: TC of rings of characteristic p
items.statement: For an E_2-ring A with p = 0 in π_0A (hence an E_2-HF_p-algebra), THH(A) is a module over THH(HF_p) in cyclotomic spectra, TC(A) → THH(A)^{hT} → THH(A)^{tT} (can − φ_p^{hT}) is a fibre sequence even without bounded below, and THH(A)^{tT} ≃ THH(A)^{hT}[v⁻¹], THH(A)^{tT}[1/p] = THH(A)^{hT}[1/p].

items.name: Symmetric monoidal ∞-categories and (lax) symmetric monoidal functors
items.statement: A symmetric monoidal ∞-category is a cocartesian fibration C^⊗ → N(Fin_*) with (ρ^i_!)_i: C^⊗_{⟨n⟩} ≃ C^n for all n; C^⊗_act = C^⊗ ×_{N(Fin_*)} N(Fin). A symmetric monoidal functor preserves all cocartesian lifts, a lax one those of inert maps; Fun_⊗(C, D) ⊆ Fun_lax(C, D) ⊆ Fun_{N(Fin_*)}(C^⊗, D^⊗).
items.note: Definitions A.1–A.2 and Remark A.3.

items.name: Symmetric monoidal Dwyer–Kan localisation
items.statement: For symmetric monoidal C^⊗ and W ⊆ C_1, W^⊗ consists of the maps over id_{⟨n⟩} that are products of maps in W; C[W⁻¹]^⊗ → N(Fin_*) is a categorical fibration with C^⊗ → C[W⁻¹]^⊗ a Dwyer–Kan localisation at W^⊗.

items.name: Hinich's theorem
items.statement: If ⊗ preserves weak equivalences in each variable: (i) C[W⁻¹]^⊗ is symmetric monoidal; (ii) i: C^⊗ → C[W⁻¹]^⊗ is symmetric monoidal; (iii) i_{⟨1⟩} is the Dwyer–Kan localisation of C at W; (iv) for every K → N(Fin_*), C[W⁻¹]^⊗ ×_{N(Fin_*)} K is the Dwyer–Kan localisation of C^⊗ ×_{N(Fin_*)} K; (v) i induces Fun_lax(C[W⁻¹], D) ≃ Fun^W_lax(C, D) and Fun_⊗(C[W⁻¹], D) ≃ Fun^W_⊗(C, D).
items.note: Hinich [50, Propositions 2.1.4, 3.2.2]. Mathlib's CategoryTheory.Localization.Monoidal (LocalizedMonoidal, at 082e2d3) is the 1-categorical analogue only.

items.name: Symmetric monoidal model categories give symmetric monoidal ∞-categories
items.statement: For a symmetric monoidal model category M: (1) N(M)[W⁻¹]^⊗ is symmetric monoidal; (2) N(M)^⊗ → N(M)[W⁻¹]^⊗ is lax symmetric monoidal; (3) its underlying functor is the Dwyer–Kan localisation of N(M); (4) the same after pullback along any K → N(Fin_*); (5) Fun_lax(N(M)[W⁻¹], D) ≃ Fun^W_lax(N(M), D); (6) N(M_c)[W⁻¹]^⊗ ≃ N(M)[W⁻¹]^⊗ symmetric monoidally.
items.note: Mathlib has model categories (HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory) but no ∞-categorical localisation.

items.name: Left derivable cocartesian fibrations
items.statement: A cocartesian fibration p: X → S with marked edges W is left derivable if p(W) are identities, each s_!: X_a → X_b has an absolute right Kan extension Ls_!: X_a[W_a⁻¹] → X_b[W_b⁻¹] of X_a → X_b → X_b[W_b⁻¹], and Lt_! ∘ Ls_! → Lu_! is an equivalence for every 2-simplex. Examples: functors preserving W (A.9), left Quillen functors and bifunctors (A.10–A.12), and N(M^⊗) → N(Fin_*) for a symmetric monoidal model category (A.13).
items.note: Definition A.8 with Examples A.9–A.13.

items.name: Localising left derivable cocartesian fibrations
items.statement: For a left derivable cocartesian fibration p: X → S: (1) X[W⁻¹] → S is a cocartesian fibration; (2) each X_a → X[W⁻¹]_a is a Dwyer–Kan localisation; (3) the induced s′_! is the absolute right Kan extension of X_a → X_b → X[W⁻¹]_b. Consequently localisation commutes with base change K → S, and X → X[W⁻¹] preserves s-cocartesian lifts when s_! preserves weak equivalences.
items.note: Proposition A.14 with Corollary A.15.

items.name: Descent for cocartesian fibrations
items.statement: (1) If X → S is cocartesian and S = colim S_i in Cat_∞, then X = colim X ×_S S_i. (2) Given cocartesian X_i → S_i forming pullback squares along the diagram, X = colim X_i → S = colim S_i is cocartesian with X_i ≃ X ×_S S_i.

items.name: Cat_∞ is generated by Δ⁰ and Δ¹
items.statement: The smallest full subcategory of Cat_∞ containing Δ⁰ and Δ¹ and closed under small colimits is Cat_∞.

items.name: Ass^⊗, cuts and Δ^op → Ass^⊗
items.statement: Ass^⊗ has the pointed finite sets as objects and maps f: ⟨n⟩ → ⟨m⟩ with linear orders on each f⁻¹(i), i ≠ 0; the functor Δ^op → Fin_* sending S to its set of cuts (S_1 ⊔ S_2 with S_1 < S_2, S ⊔ ∅ ~ ∅ ⊔ S the base point) lifts to Δ^op → Ass^⊗.
items.locator: Appendix B, Appendix B (Ass^⊗ and cuts), p. 379

items.name: The paracyclic and cyclic categories
items.statement: Λ_∞ ⊆ ZPoSet is the full subcategory of objects isomorphic to (1/n)Z, n ≥ 1, with Z-equivariant non-decreasing maps; BZ acts by f ↦ f + 1, Λ_p = Λ_∞/B(pZ) for 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞, and Λ = Λ_1 is Connes's cyclic category; Λ_∞ is self-dual (f ↦ f^∨, f^∨(x) = min{y : f(y) ≥ x}), BZ-equivariantly.
items.locator: Appendix B, Appendix B (Λ_∞, Λ_p, Λ), p. 380
items.note: The libraries have no cyclic category (audit of RT.1).

items.name: The cyclic category over Ass^⊗_act, and Δ as a slice
items.statement: V: Λ → Fin, T ↦ T/Z, refines to V: Λ → Ass^⊗_act (Proposition B.1); Λ_{/[1]_Λ} → Δ is an equivalence (Corollary B.2), giving j: Δ^op → Λ^op, [n] ↦ [n+1]_Λ, which factors through j_∞: Δ^op → Λ_∞^op.
items.note: Proposition B.1 and Corollary B.2.

items.name: Δ^op → Λ_∞^op is cofinal
items.statement: The functor j_∞: NΔ^op → NΛ_∞^op is cofinal; hence NΛ_∞^op is sifted, |NΛ_∞| is contractible and |NΛ| = |NΛ_∞|/BZ ≃ BBZ = K(Z, 2) = BT ≃ CP^∞.
items.note: Theorem B.3 and Corollary B.4. The printed covering argument has a gap (sourceIssues PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18/E2); the statement is true.

items.name: Realisation of cyclic objects carries a circle action
items.statement: For C with geometric realisations there is a natural functor Fun(N(Λ^op), C) → C^{BT} whose underlying object is colim_{N(Δ^op)} j*F; likewise for Λ_p^op-objects (BC_p-equivariantly, Lemma B.18) and for BC_p-equivariant functors N(Λ_p^op) → C^{BT} (Proposition B.22).
items.note: RT.2 plans the S¹-action on THH as coherent data.

items.name: Geometric realisation of simplicial and paracyclic spaces
items.statement: |Δ^S| = Hom_Int(S^∨, [0, 1]) with S^∨ = Hom_Δ(S, [1]) (increasing coordinates) gives |−|: Fun(Δ^op, Top) → Top as a coend; |Λ_∞^T| = {Z-equivariant non-decreasing T^∨ → R} gives a BZ-equivariant |−|: Fun(Λ_∞^op, Top) → RTop, and for cyclic spaces a T = R/Z-action; |Δ^S| × R ≅ |Λ_∞^{j_∞(S)}|, and the underlying space of |X| is |j_∞^*X|.
items.note: Construction B.6, Construction B.9, Example B.10, Remark B.11, Lemma B.12.

items.name: Proper simplicial spaces realise to colimits
items.statement: On proper simplicial spaces (latching inclusions h-cofibrations), |−| agrees with the ∞-categorical colimit: N Fun(Δ^op, Top)_prop → N Top over Fun(N(Δ^op), S) → S commutes up to natural equivalence.

items.name: Realisation of proper paracyclic and cyclic spaces and spectra
items.statement: For proper paracyclic spaces the square N Fun(Λ_∞^op, Top)_prop → N RTop over Fun(N(Λ_∞^op), S) → S commutes BZ-equivariantly (Proposition B.13); for cyclic spaces with values in TTop and S^{BT} (Corollary B.14); and the same for (para)cyclic orthogonal spectra (Proposition B.15, Corollary B.16), with BC_p-equivariant variants (Lemma B.18, Propositions B.21–B.22).

items.name: Edgewise subdivision
items.statement: sd_p: Λ_p → Λ, [n]_{Λ_p} ↦ [pn]_Λ, induces |Λ_p| ≃ |Λ|; for C with geometric realisations, realisation of X and of sd_p^*X agree, and for proper paracyclic spaces or spectra |X| ≅ |sd_p^*X| T-equivariantly.
items.note: Proposition B.17 (compatibility with self-duality) and Proposition B.19.

items.name: Tate construction and realisation
items.statement: There is a natural transformation from Fun(Λ_p^op, Sp) → Fun(Λ^op, Sp) → Sp^{BT} (levelwise −^{tC_p}, then realisation) to Fun(Λ_p^op, Sp) → Sp^{BT} → Sp^{B(T/C_p)} ≃ Sp^{BT} (realisation, then −^{tC_p}).

items.name: Geometric realisation preserves finite limits
items.statement: In compactly generated weak Hausdorff spaces, |−|: Fun(Δ^op, Top) → Top commutes with finite limits.

items.name: Gluing lemma for spaces
items.statement: Given B ← A → C and B′ ← A′ → C′ with A → B and A′ → B′ h-cofibrations and levelwise weak homotopy equivalences between them, B ∪_A C → B′ ∪_{A′} C′ is a weak homotopy equivalence.
items.note: Boardman–Vogt [20, Proposition 4.8(b)].

items.name: Realisation of proper simplicial spaces is homotopical
items.statement: A levelwise weak homotopy equivalence of proper simplicial spaces realises to a weak homotopy equivalence.
items.note: H.2 plans the levelwise-equivalence theorem under cofibrancy hypotheses.

items.name: Bousfield–Kan homotopy colimits of spaces
items.statement: hocolim_I X = |[n] ↦ ∐_{i_0→…→i_n} X(i_0)|; it is homotopical and models the ∞-categorical colimit. For pointed diagrams the reduced hocolim is hocolim_I X / hocolim_I pt, homotopical on well-pointed diagrams and modelling the colimit of pointed spaces.
items.note: Definitions C.4, C.6, Propositions C.5, C.7; printed with X(i_n) (sourceIssues PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18/E18).

items.name: Homotopy colimits of orthogonal spectra
items.statement: The gluing lemma holds for orthogonal spectra along h-cofibrations and stable equivalences (Lemma C.8, not for pointed spaces); the levelwise reduced hocolim of orthogonal spectra (Definition C.10) is homotopical for all diagrams, well-pointed or not, and models the ∞-categorical colimit (Proposition C.11).
items.note: Lemma C.8 (Mandell–May), Remark C.9, Definition C.10, Proposition C.11.

items.name: Fixed points commute with realisations and hocolims
items.statement: hocolim_I commutes with geometric realisation (Lemma C.12); for a finite group (or compact Lie group) G, −^G: GSp^O → Sp^O commutes with geometric realisations and homotopy colimits up to homeomorphism (Lemma C.13); and hocolim_I of orthogonal G-spectra is homotopical for equivariant equivalences and models the colimit in GSp (Proposition C.14).
items.note: Lemma C.12, Lemma C.13, Proposition C.14.

coverage.policy: Every definition, construction, theorem, proposition, lemma and corollary is an item, with closely linked statements merged and named in the note (for example Definitions II.2.2–II.2.3 and Proposition II.2.4). Remarks and examples are items when they state mathematics used later (Examples I.1.12, I.2.3, II.1.2, IV.1.2; Remark III.1.6); purely expository remarks are not.

routes.reason: RT.2 plans exactly this paper's subject: THH of E_1-algebras by cyclic realisation with the circle action as coherent data, homotopy orbits, homotopy fixed points and Tate constructions with the norm sequence and multiplicative structure, cyclotomic spectra as Frobenius maps to Tate constructions, TC, TC⁻ and TP with the bounded-below fixed-point formula, and agreement with the classical genuine-equivariant TR/TC. The paper is the canonical source for all of it and more than RT.2 names: the Tate orbit and fixpoint lemmas, the uniqueness of the multiplicative structure, the Farrell–Tate construction for the circle, the lax equalizer, the Tate diagonal, the genuine-equivariant background needed for the classical comparison (orthogonal G-spectra, geometric fixed points, Borel completion, isotropy separation), the coalgebra argument behind Theorem II.6.9, the Bökstedt construction and the comparison of the two THH, the cyclic and paracyclic categories with their realisations, and the E_∞ and loop-space examples. The planned items included (Corollary 1.5, Definitions II.1.1, II.1.6, II.1.8, Theorems II.4.10–II.4.11 and others) are ones for which this paper is the source RT.2's design should follow.

RT.1 owns algebraic Hochschild homology and plans HKR only for smooth algebras in characteristic 0. Proposition IV.4.1 is the derived HKR filtration for every commutative ring, built from the cotangent complex and derived exterior powers of DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0; Proposition IV.4.3, HH(F_p) as a divided power algebra, follows from it.

E5:abstract plans symmetric monoidal ∞-categories as cocartesian fibrations over Fin_*, operadic algebras, monoidal functors and stable categories, and E5:presentability Ind-completion; StableHomotopyKTheory, GeneralAlgebraicKTheory and RefinedTraceMethods all draw on this single supplier. The paper's Appendix A (Hinich's symmetric monoidal Dwyer–Kan localisation, symmetric monoidal model categories, left derivable cocartesian fibrations), the Verdier quotients of §I.3 with their symmetric monoidal version, and the envelope Fun_⊗(C^⊗_act, D) ≃ Fun_lax(C, D) of Proposition III.3.2 are general ∞-categorical statements that belong there, not in a trace roadmap.

H.1 plans nerves and their geometric realisation, and H.2 the levelwise-equivalence theorem and bisimplicial realisation under cofibrancy hypotheses. The paper's facts about geometric realisation of proper simplicial spaces in compactly generated weak Hausdorff spaces (commuting with finite limits, the gluing lemma, homotopy invariance, agreement with the ∞-categorical colimit) and the Bousfield–Kan homotopy colimit of spaces are these layers' concerns; the spectrum-level and equivariant versions stay with RT.2, which alone needs them.

L.5 plans THH, TR and TC of perfect fields. §IV.4 computes THH(F_p)^{hT}, THH(F_p)^{tT}, the Frobenius and TC(F_p) from Bökstedt periodicity alone, identifies THH(F_p) as the E_∞-cyclotomic spectrum sh_p(HZ_p^triv), and gives the characteristic-p fibre sequence; these are sources for L.5's calculation, and Bökstedt periodicity and the TC(F_p) computation, already planned there, are included.

routes.title: Homotopy foundations for algebraic K-theory, Part II: power operations and the Segal conjecture for C_p
routes.brief: Design PowerOperationsAndSegalConjecture, the Part II of Homotopy foundations for algebraic K-theory (StableHomotopyKTheory), following Nikolaus–Scholze, On topological cyclic homology (Acta Math. 221 (2018)), §§III.1 and IV.1, and the classical inputs they cite. Final theorems, as the paper states them (with its misprints corrected): Theorem III.1.7 — for every bounded below spectrum X, the Tate diagonal Δ_p: X → (X ⊗ … ⊗ X)^{tC_p} exhibits the target as the p-completion of X, which fails without the bounded below hypothesis ((KU ⊗ KU)^{tC_2} is rational); Theorem IV.1.15 with Proposition IV.1.16 — the Tate-valued Frobenius HF_p → (HF_p^{tC_p})^{hF_p^×} is the product of the Steenrod squares Sq^i: HF_2 → HF_2[i] for p = 2, and of P^i: HF_p → HF_p[2i(p−1)] and βP^i: HF_p → HF_p[2i(p−1)+1] for odd p (the printed shifts [i(p−1)] are misprints), with the HZ variant through reduction; Theorem IV.1.21 — postcomposition with Σ^nφ_R is Rezk's degree-n power operation R^n(X) → R^{n·ρ}(BΣ_p × X) followed by can; Proposition IV.1.12 — the Tate-valued Frobenius of KU is the Adams operation ψ^p on KU⁰(X) ⊗ Q_p and, as a map KU → KU_p^∧[1/p] ≃ (KU^{tC_p})^{hF_p^×}, the stable ψ^p followed by completion (β ↦ pβ); Theorem IV.3.7 — for simply connected Y the Frobenius of THH(S[ΩY]) = Σ^∞_+LY is a p-completion and (Σ^∞_+LY)^{C_{p^n}} → (Σ^∞_+LY)^{hC_{p^n}} is a p-adic equivalence. Cover: the Segal conjecture for C_p (S → S^{tC_p} is a p-completion; Lin for p = 2, Gunawardena for odd p), with what it needs — the mod p Steenrod algebra, the Adams spectral sequence for inverse limits of spectra, Lin's Ext computation or the Singer construction; the HF_p case HF_p ≃ (HF_p^{⊗p})^{tC_p} (Lunøe-Nielsen–Rognes, the topological Singer construction); the reduction from HF_p to all bounded below X (Postnikov truncation, Lemma I.2.6, the pro-isomorphism Lemma III.1.8); extended powers and twisted cohomology R^{n·ρ}(X × BΣ_p) through Thom spectra of parametrised spectra (Lemma IV.1.19), Rezk's power operations and Lemmas IV.1.3, IV.1.7, IV.1.17–IV.1.20 with Corollaries IV.1.8–IV.1.10; the Steenrod operations as the components of the power operation of HF_p ([BMMS, VIII.2]); Atiyah's cyclic power operation in K-theory; the examples S^{hC_p} and KU of Example I.2.3 and the spherical Witt vectors of Example IV.1.2; and Kuhn's convergence for Σ^∞_+ of the cosimplicial model of LY, Y simply connected. Import rather than re-plan: from Hochschild, cyclotomic and refined trace methods (RefinedTraceMethods) RT.2, the Tate construction and its multiplicativity, the Tate diagonal with its uniqueness and lax symmetric monoidal structure, the Tate-valued Frobenius, cyclotomic spectra and THH(S[ΩY]) ≃ Σ^∞_+LY, and from RT.4:topological the spectrum KU and Bott periodicity; from this roadmap's H.5 and H.6, spectra, p-completion, Postnikov towers and spectral sequences with their convergence; from Enhanced derived categories of sheaves (EnhancedDerivedSheaves) E5:abstract, symmetric monoidal ∞-categories and E_∞-rings; from the Tau Ceti roadmap Algebraic topology of spaces and manifolds (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology, stage 6) singular cohomology with cup products. Keep the bounded below hypothesis of Theorem III.1.7 visible, and state the Segal conjecture only for C_p: the paper claims nothing for other finite groups.
routes.reason: The paper's generalised Segal conjecture (Theorem III.1.7) rests on the Segal conjecture for C_p and the Lunøe-Nielsen–Rognes computation for HF_p, both Adams-spectral-sequence calculations; §IV.1 identifies the Tate-valued Frobenius with Steenrod and Adams operations through power operations. Nothing in the atlas plans the Steenrod algebra, the Adams spectral sequence, extended powers or power operations, and RT.2 needs none of them to construct cyclotomic spectra or TC. StableHomotopyKTheory owns spectra, p-completion and spectral sequences (H.5, H.6), so these computations extend it in its own direction; its summary disclaims 'all of stable homotopy theory', hence a Part II rather than new layers in it.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition II.3.4 and its proof, p. 259 (also arXiv v2)
sourceIssues.printed: There is a natural functor Cyc Sp^gen → Cyc Sp = Sp^{BT} ×_{∏_{p∈P} Sp^{BC_{p^∞}}} ∏_{p∈P} Cyc Sp_p. … The induced functor Cyc Sp^gen → ∏_{p∈P} Sp^{BC_{p^∞}} lifts to a functor Cyc Sp^gen → Sp^{BT} by looking at the underlying spectrum with T-action
sourceIssues.correction: Drop the identification. Cyc Sp (Definition II.1.6(i)) asks each φ_p to be T ≅ T/C_p-equivariant, while the fibre product only records φ_p as a C_{p^∞}-equivariant map. The natural functor Cyc Sp^gen → Cyc Sp does exist: it is the one of §II.6, Cyc Sp^gen ⊆ CoAlg_{(Φ^{C_p})}(TSp_F) → CoAlg_{(−^{tC_p})}(Sp^{BT}) ≃ Cyc Sp (Lemma II.5.8), where the residual T/C_p-action on Φ^{C_p}X makes each Frobenius T-equivariant. On bounded below objects X^{tC_p} is p-complete (Lemma I.2.9) and C_{p^∞} → T is a p-adic equivalence, as the proof of Theorem II.4.11 uses, so there the two notions of Frobenius agree.
sourceIssues.reason: Both sides are categorical fibrations over Sp^{BT}, so an equivalence would give equivalences of fibres. Over X = KU with trivial T-action the fibres are ∏_p Ω^∞W_p^{hT} and ∏_p Ω^∞W_p^{hC_{p^∞}}, with W_p = map(KU, KU^{tC_p}). W_p is a rational KU-module, as KU^{tC_p} is rational (Example I.2.3(iii)), so W_p^{hC_{p^∞}} ≃ W_p, BC_{p^∞} being rationally a point. The fibre of W_p^{hT} → W_p is Σ^{−2}W_p^{hT} (Gysin sequence; W_p is complex oriented), and W_p^{hT} ≠ 0 because the non-zero map KU → KU^{hC_p} → KU^{tC_p} is T-equivariant (as in Example II.1.2(ii)). Being 2-periodic, Σ^{−2}W_p^{hT} has non-zero homotopy in non-negative degrees, so Ω^∞W_p^{hT} → Ω^∞W_p is not an equivalence. The authors' Remark II.1.3 notes the same difference between T- and C_{p^∞}-equivariant Frobenius maps outside the p-complete bounded below case.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem B.3, p. 383 (also arXiv v2)
sourceIssues.printed: We now apply this criterion to the ∞-category C = Δ/T = Δ ×_{Λ∞} Λ∞/T with the 'covering' given by U_t := C[t, t+1), t ∈ T, where C[a, b) … consists of pairs (S, ϕ) … such that ϕ(S) ⊆ [a, b) ⊆ T. … Finite intersections of U_t's are always also of the form C[a, b), where b ⩽ a+1. … It follows that U1 ∪...∪Un is also weakly contractible
sourceIssues.correction: Use closed intervals U_t = C[t, t+1], which do cover C: a simplex (S_0, ϕ_0) → … → (S_k, ϕ_k) has all ϕ_i(S_i) inside ϕ_k(S_k) ⊆ [ϕ_k(min), ϕ_k(min) + 1]. For a ≤ b ≤ a + 1, C[a, b] ≅ Δ/[k] (k + 1 the number of points of T in [a, b]) has a terminal object. Add the U_t for consecutive t_0 < t_1 < … of T ∩ [−N, N] in increasing order: (U_{t_0} ∪ … ∪ U_{t_{n−1}}) ∩ U_{t_n} = C[t_n, t_{n−1} + 1] is contractible, so each window is weakly contractible by the pushout step, and C is the filtered union of the windows. The last line of the induction should read U_0 ∪ … ∪ U_n.
sourceIssues.reason: The half-open U_t do not cover C: for T = Z (n = 1) and S = [1], ϕ(k, 0) = k, ϕ(k, 1) = k + 1 is non-decreasing and Z-equivariant on Z × [1], but ϕ({0} × S) = {0, 1} lies in no [t, t + 1). And the criterion needs every finite intersection weakly contractible, while U_0 ∩ U_1 = C[1, 1) is empty (so is any C[a, b) with b ≤ a, which the reduction to Δ/[k−1] with k ≥ 1 silently excludes). The theorem is true, by the argument above.
